quest.title: Return to the Moon
quest.description: It's time to begin the journey home...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VI
chapter.title: Melting Moonlight in the Morning Mist

talks.objective: Set out on the path back to the moon
Set out on the path back to the moon

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: This is... this is where the people of Hyperborea used to communicate with the moons...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Eternal Moon, Frost Moon, Iridescent Moon... When the power of all three converge...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The gate to the moons shall open.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Mmhmm...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The Moon Marrows are in position. Only the final step remains.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I'm sure Nasha Town is livelier than ever at this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... It's a shame you couldn't be there for it. But it's now or never, right?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's fine. I'm more than happy with this... my last piece of luggage — my only piece of luggage.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I can already feel the moon calling to me.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: This ray of light will lead you home, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: From now on, we will at last have a reason to pray to the true moon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be sure to come back and see us when you get the chance!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hah... Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if that chance doesn't come... Then remember that you have friends on this planet — people who will miss "Columbina."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes, I will. Thank you for everything you've done for me.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And remember... Come night or day, the moonlight shall always connect us.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ... Well then... Farewell, my friends.

talks.objective: Set out on the path back to the moon
Discuss what to do with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Are you alright? Do your wounds still hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I had someone prepare a little medicine that could prove effective. Take it if you need to.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: In that case, let me relate the contents of the call we made to Alice after the incident occurred.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: That Dottore is a crafty one... He distracted the Hexenzirkel by creating a huge fuss at Teyvat's borders.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I'd assumed that the cause was an Abyssal intrusion from the outside world — which, in fairness, is a rather common occurrence.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But after learning that you managed to influence the phantoms in Nod-Krai, I realized that perhaps this interference could have come from within Teyvat instead.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But we weren't able to change their fates...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: True, you couldn't change how their stories ended. But you did build some "variables" around yourself.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Variables?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Yes — things you heard that you could not otherwise have learned, ideas that would otherwise have never crossed your mind... All these things are "variables."

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Of course, most variables usually pale into insignificance with the myriad of possibilities floating around. But the moment you start treating them as building blocks and intentionally stacking them, that changes things.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: That's what Dottore did, and it's how he created the necessary conditions so that when you activated the portal tonight, it played right into his plan.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: However, we have no way of knowing exactly what he did.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yeah. We also need to ascertain Columbina's status.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: And that about sums it up.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As I suspected, Dottore has disappeared completely. If it's any consolation, he wasn't able to control Columbina as he might have wished to.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm afraid that's small consolation, given the reason why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? She did what!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, didn't any of you see her do that...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All we saw was, Dottore appeared and used some kind of power... The next thing we knew, he and Columbina were gone, and you were falling into the sea.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I see... The Doctor froze time, which is why only I could move freely.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (From their perspective, the battle and Columbina's decision all happened in a single instant.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So that's the power of the three moons? But why wasn't I affected? ...Is it because I'm a Descender?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So, Columbina intentionally opened the Moon Gate, and escaped into the same mysterious world as Rerir and Tholindis...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sounds like bad news.

choices.text: This must be why Dottore's been lying low this whole time.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Seen in that way, the "Trilunar Syzygy" and Rerir's emergence... Dottore might have been pulling the strings in both cases.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: According to Miss Alice, he is attempting to transcend his destiny and finish an experiment that only a god might complete.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...An utter lunatic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec, where's Hat Guy? Seems like he'd wanna be here for this.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: He took off with the Dodocommunication Device after we spoke to Alice. He said he had a hunch that he wanted to investigate by himself.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The look on his face was terrifying... I've never seen him like that before.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Probably anger and frustration at the fact that Dottore was one step ahead, despite his best efforts.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And honestly, I feel the same way...)

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'm back.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hat Guy!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I went to look for the Hyperborean phantoms again. I think I've gotten to the bottom of it.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I got them to talk to Nicole on the other end of the communications line. Turns out, the history they describe is different from how Nicole remembers it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? But how? Surely Nicole can't have been wrong...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Because the phantoms are the ones who were deceived. They speak of a "savior" who appeared in their history, one who never should've existed.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: This savior promised to create a new moon within the false sky, and even bring back their Moon Goddesses.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Foolishly, they believed in him, and told him everything he wanted to know about the moons.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It's obvious that this was Dottore's doing.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Now you mention it... The first time we entered the Hyperborean ruins, we heard the phantoms discussing their history, and I remember Nicole commenting that something sounded a little strange...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Dottore shouldn't have been able to get in there in the first place!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: He didn't. Nicole said that this was an anomalous state triggered by disruptions in the causal connections between phantoms from the same era.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: The "variables" that Dottore put in place were substantial enough that they even affected phantoms that he never met.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So it's not that their memories were unclear... they'd been tampered with.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That's exactly the possibility Dottore was trying to manufacture. He turned these variables into knowledge and engineered the situation so all that knowledge would fall into his hands.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Then, he harnessed that knowledge on Moon-Prayer Night... to truly create a "false moon."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How is that even possible?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: To be precise, he exploited a weakness in the way the spell works.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: The spell senses kuuvahki to detect the moon's location. So, as long as the "false moon" more strongly resembled a moon than the Frost Moon beyond the skies...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That gate would teleport Columbina to the false moon's location... in other words, to Dottore's side.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Once he had her under control, the teleportation spell remained active, and he manipulated her power to seize both Moon Marrows.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: At that moment, the Moon Marrows disappeared right before our eyes... It was already too late even as we were leaving the ruins.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: By then, Dottore had already amassed the power of all three moons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Where does this leave us? What do we do now?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'd certainly like to know what Her Majesty thinks, now that the concerns I expressed to her have come to pass. But we cannot simply sit and wait for her to decide the matter.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: And in any case, it is not the Fatui Harbinger, "Damselette," who sees us as her friends, but rather, Columbina Hyposelenia.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: If, even in such extreme circumstances, Her Majesty will not lift the prohibition on Harbingers drawing steel against one another...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Then I will do as my heart demands. I will fight as Peruere instead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arlecchino...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Time is short, so I'll make the first move.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, even Arlecchino seems to be losing her cool now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I'm sure she feels partly responsible for this... And so do I...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright, alright, alright. Lose those dejected looks for a moment, and let me get a word in.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It looks bad, I won't lie. Very bad, in fact.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So Dottore's pulled some real dirty tricks to gain the upper hand — for now.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And yeah, it's to the point where even the mages say that his "variables" have affected destiny. I'm not so sure, though.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Many have told me that Teyvat's destiny is fixed, and that does appear to be the case. Well, what makes Dottore so sure he'll be the exception?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And since he was able to stack these "variables" up, who's to say we can't do the same?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You, of all people, should not be discouraged, traveler from afar.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: This isn't over yet.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And you're not alone in that. Everyone here does, whether they've spoken thus far or not.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But none of us are the type to sit back and wait for the sun to shine again.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's exactly how a knight should roll — they knock you down, you get back up and get back in it. Don't forget, Honorary Knight, you're a legitimate member of Mondstadt, too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Varka's right! This is far from over!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dottore's already way overdue a butt-kicking given his past shenanigans. And after this, he's earned himself a double dose!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's what I'm talking about!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: How's everyone else feeling?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I'll use kuuvahki to investigate Columbina's whereabouts. I'm not ready to give up either.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Leave the intel-gathering to me. Whatever happens within Nod-Krai's borders, when the Curatorium of Secrets wants to be in the know, we always find a way.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Aino and I will do all we can to support you. We will attempt to reverse engineer Dottore's actions and seek a breakthrough that way.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Alice and Nicole are busy dealing with an emergency at Teyvat's borders, so they can't return just yet...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But they're both very angry about this. They've asked Albedo and me to act on the Hexenzirkel's behalf and do everything in our power to fight back against Dottore.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Are you ready, then? We're going to have to conduct a lot of research, even in the early stages.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I'll do my best.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: As for me, I'm pretty familiar with Dottore's way of doing things, so I can try to predict his next move. I'll help with your investigation.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Nice. Looks like we have our basic division of labor.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'll get in touch with Flins and Illuga, get them to have a chat with their Starshyna. Couldn't hurt to bring the Lightkeepers on board as well.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: At the same time, I'll pass on instructions to the Knights present in Nod-Krai to assist the Lightkeepers and other organizations in ensuring the safety of those living here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We'll show him!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's it, then. Good luck, everyone.

choices.text: We've got to be prepared for anything.
Still... I can't help but blame myself.
...He was biding time until he could execute his plan.
But I'd rather talk about what just happened...

talks.objective: Go outside and gaze at the moon

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Columbina...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I never thought that "Columbina" would become my real name.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: It went being from a Fatui codename... to "something my friends call me."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (I still don't know what to expect on the moon...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (Will I really be able to send messages to my friends...?)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (I wonder where I'll be when the next Moon-Prayer Night comes?)
